messages:
Alex (CS): quick recap from week1 smoke for Nimbus private deploy — posting sticky snags and next steps. main areas: KMS key policy, subnet egress routes, and renewal signal for reserved capacity.
Maria (Eng): saw the KMS key reject errors in the logs around 09:12 UTC — likely key policy is missing the service principal from our side. stack trace snippet in logs looked like `AccessDeniedException: Unable to decrypt` repeatedly.
Jordan (Customer): yep we hit that when exercising model load. can confirm our IAM role used for inference is `nimbus-llm-exec`.
Sam (Infra): probing their policy now. quick checklist: 1) key arn matches 2) kms:Decrypt on role 3) grant for cross-account usage. can you paste the key arn?
Jordan (Customer): arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:987654321012:key/3a4b5c6d-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-abcdef123456
Maria (Eng): thanks. Sam — when you add the grant please also include `kms:GenerateDataKey*` for the workload, otherwise cache warming fails.
Sam (Infra): on it. small note on networking: we observed intermittent timeouts when TLS handshake with our model-serving mesh started from their private subnets. probable culprit: missing route for the egress NAT in the private subnet that touches the inference node.
Alex (CS): Jordan — do you control the NAT gateway for the private subnets or do we need to coordinate with your net team?
Jordan (Customer): our net team manages VPC. I'll ping them. cc @netops. they told me earlier they only allow specific destination ports outbound.
Maria (Eng): that aligns — model registry fetch uses https on 443 and gRPC on 8443. If outbound is restricted to 443 only, we'll need an allow for 8443 or proxy traffic through 443.
Sam (Infra): short-term workaround: set the model fetch to use our HTTPS proxy on 443. I'll share proxy host. longer-term we should get a dedicated egress rule.
Alex (CS): action items: Sam to add KMS grant + share `grant-id`; Sam to share proxy host; Jordan to escalate NAT/egress rule with netops; Maria to validate with a smoke run after grants and proxy are in. ETA EOD tomorrow.
Sam (Infra): KMS grant created: grant-id = `g-0a1b2c3d4e`. Added `kms:Decrypt` and `kms:GenerateDataKey*` for role `arn:aws:iam::987654321012:role/nimbus-llm-exec`. Pasted policy snippet:
```json
{"GranteePrincipal":"arn:aws:iam::987654321012:role/nimbus-llm-exec","Operations":["Decrypt","GenerateDataKey","GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext"]}
```
Sam (Infra): proxy host: `proxy-usw2.redwood-infra.internal:443`. Maria try setting `MODEL_FETCH_PROXY` to that in env.
Maria (Eng): starting a targeted smoke now using `MODEL_FETCH_PROXY`. running script: `./smoke.sh --model=my-runner --region=us-west-2`. will report back in ~12m.
deploy-bot: deployment notification — canary rollout v2 -> v2b started (id: canary-176543).
Maria (Eng): smoke result: model fetch ok, KMS decrypt ok, but we hit an audit-log gap — the customer's Splunk endpoint didn't get the full `request_id` field from our side, shows `null` occasionally. suspect a truncation during log-forwarder batching.
Alex (CS): noted. Jordan, this touches observability + compliance — does your audit team require full request_id for retention policies?
Jordan (Customer): yes, compliance requires immutable `request_id` mapping for 90 days. partial ids are a blocker for our SOC signoff.
Sam (Infra): can roll an update to forwarder to include the full `request_id` field. low-risk patch. I can stage it in their staging relay.
Alex (CS): new action items appended: Sam to patch forwarder and stage; Maria to re-run smoke after patch; Jordan to confirm SOC acceptance criteria and share any sample logging schema.
Jordan (Customer): will share schema and a quick SOC checklist by EOD. thanks all. :thumbsup:
Alex (CS): thanks team — rolling these into the week1 health doc and renewal flag: moderate. we flagged a potential renewal risk if audit logging or KMS policy issues aren't closed within 2 weeks. I'll update the account health dashboard and loop in AM.
Maria (Eng): one more technical note: we saw increased p99 latency (~120ms -> 240ms) when the proxy was used for model pulls; this is acceptable for cold-starts but if they want bursty loads we'll recommend pre-warming and a modest dedicated capacity commit.
Alex (CS): great callout — I'll put that into the Optimize recommendations and cost/latency tradeoffs doc for Nimbus.
Sam (Infra): patch and proxy config pushed to their staging. will notify when prod-ready.
Alex (CS): closing thread for now — will re-open if smoke fails or if SOC schema delayed. thanks everyone.
